documents.summary: University-wide guidelines from the University Teaching Council on AI in teaching and learning. They leave course rules to instructors and departments and list categories of expected use, while setting rules on syllabus statements, acknowledgement and citation, privacy and review.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines set no single university rule on student AI use. They say instructors 'should make clear statements in syllabi' and offer categories from 'Require students to use AI' to 'Forbid use of AI', and say departments 'should determine' how to incorporate AI, so the decision is handed to instructors and units.

units.fit_note: Describes generative AI generally rather than offering a formal definition clause.

documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) - Guidance on Use
documents.summary: System IT guidance on acceptable and legal use of generative AI across UMS: no personal or protected data in tools, copyright and acceptable-use limits, bias and accuracy checks, disclosure by faculty and staff, and accessibility. It is explicitly not policy and is not specific to teaching.
documents.stance_why: The guidance does not ban or hand off AI use; it refers to 'uses of generative AI that are not prohibited' and sets conditions such as no protected data, review for accuracy and disclosure. That is permission with conditions, so permit rather than delegates.
documents.stance_resolution_why: Coder A coded permit, coder B delegates.
